title: Tensor products commute with filtered colimits of (ring, module, module) systems
statement:
Let $I$ be a directed set, $(A_i,\alpha_{ij})_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings, and $(M_i,\mu_{ij})$, $(N_i,
u_{ij})$ directed systems of abelian groups over $I$ such that each $M_i$, $N_i$ is an $A_i$-module and the transition maps are semilinear: $\mu_{ij}(am)=\alpha_{ij}(a)\mu_{ij}(m)$, $
u_{ij}(an)=\alpha_{ij}(a)
u_{ij}(n)$ for $i\le j$. Let $A=\varinjlim A_i$, $M=\varinjlim M_i$, $N=\varinjlim N_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with coprojections $\alpha_i,\mu_i,
u_i$, and make $M,N$ into $A$-modules by $\alpha_i(a)\mu_i(m)=\mu_i(am)$, $\alpha_i(a)
u_i(n)=
u_i(an)$ (well defined since $I$ is directed). The groups $T_i=M_i\otimes_{A_i}N_i$ form a directed system with transition maps $m\otimes n\mapsto\mu_{ij}(m)\otimes
u_{ij}(n)$ (each $T_j$ regarded as an $A_i$-module via $\alpha_{ij}$), and $T=\varinjlim T_i$ with coprojections $\lambda_i$ is an $A$-module by $\alpha_i(a)\lambda_i(t)=\lambda_i(at)$. Then there is a unique homomorphism $\psi:T	o M\otimes_AN$ with $\psi(\lambda_i(m\otimes n))=\mu_i(m)\otimes
u_i(n)$ for all $i$, $m\in M_i$, $n\in N_i$, and $\psi$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. Moreover $\psi$ is natural: for morphisms of such systems $(f_i:M_i	o M'_i)$, $(g_i:N_i	o N'_i)$ ($A_i$-linear, compatible with the transition maps) one has $\psi'\circ\varinjlim(f_i\otimes g_i)=(\varinjlim f_i\otimes\varinjlim g_i)\circ\psi$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 007K (lemma-stalk-tensor-presheaf-modules, Section 6.15, proof omitted: this lemma is its algebraic content for the directed set of neighbourhoods); the fixed-ring case is Algebra, Lemma 10.12.9 (Tag 00DD, lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits, literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex line 1932, whose second direct proof is the model for the varying-ring case)

proof.text:
*The canonical map.* The semilinearity hypotheses make $m\otimes n\mapsto\mu_{ij}(m)\otimes
u_{ij}(n)$ balanced over $A_i$, so the displayed maps define a directed system $(T_i)$. The maps $(m,n)\mapsto\mu_i(m)\otimes
u_i(n)$ are $A_i$-balanced: for $a\in A_i$, both sides are $\alpha_i(a)(\mu_i(m)\otimes
u_i(n))$. They therefore induce compatible homomorphisms $T_i	o M\otimes_A N$, and the universal property of the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives the unique $A$-linear map $\psi:T	o M\otimes_A N$ with the stated formula. The same balancedness check shows that the displayed formulas define the claimed $A$-module structures on $M$, $N$, and $T$; directedness supplies a common later stage whenever two representatives are compared.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 007K; the universal-property construction is the first part of the omitted algebraic proof

proof.text:
*Surjectivity.* Every pure tensor in $M\otimes_A N$ is represented by $\mu_i(m)\otimes
u_j(n)$ for some stages $i,j$. Choose $k$ receiving maps from both stages. Then this tensor equals $\mu_k(\mu_{ik}(m))\otimes
u_k(
u_{jk}(n))$, which is the image under $\psi$ of the class of $\mu_{ik}(m)\otimes
u_{jk}(n)\in T_k$. Since pure tensors generate the tensor product, $\psi$ is surjective.

source.place: Lemma 10.12.9 (Tag 00DD), second direct proof: generators of a tensor product and a common later index

proof.text: *Injectivity: relations from one stage.* Represent an element of $T$ by a finite sum of tensors from finitely many stages, and move all terms to one common stage $k$. If its image under $\psi$ is zero, the resulting finite sum in $M\otimes_A N$ is a finite consequence of additivity and of relations $ar\otimes s-r\otimes as$ with $a$ represented at some stage. Move the finitely many coefficients and tensors occurring in this relation to one still later stage $\ell$. Semilinearity identifies the original element with the image of the corresponding balanced relation in $T_\ell$, hence its class in $T$ is zero. This is exactly the common-stage argument in Tag 00DD, with the coefficient ring allowed to advance along the directed system; the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies the common-stage class with the original class.

source.place: Lemma 10.12.9 (Tag 00DD), second direct proof, adapted to a directed system of coefficient rings

proof.text: *Inverse and naturality.* The preceding construction gives a two-sided inverse by sending a pure tensor $\mu_i(m)\otimes\nu_i(n)$ to the class of $m\otimes n$ in $T$; the common-stage argument proves that this is well defined and balanced over $A$. It is inverse to $\psi$ on the generators of both tensor products, so $\psi$ is an isomorphism. For compatible $A_i$-linear maps $f_i,g_i$, both composites in the naturality square send the generator $\lambda_i(m\otimes n)$ to $\mu'_i(f_i(m))\otimes\nu'_i(g_i(n))$; generation by such elements proves equality.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 007K; naturality follows from the same generator calculation

proof_origin.place: Lemma 10.12.9 (Tag 00DD), second direct proof, with the coefficient ring advanced to a common stage; the application to sheaf stalks is Sheaves Lemma 007K

split_report.summary: Parent proof written in four steps following the algebraic content of Stacks Sheaves Lemma 007K and the common-stage tensor argument of Algebra Lemma 10.12.9 (Tag 00DD). No child proof nodes were created: the universal-property construction, common-stage surjectivity and injectivity, inverse, and naturality are carried by this parent. The existing def-weil-pbc-category-colimit is the sole proof dependency; Mathlib searches record that no varying-ring tensor-colimit theorem exists.
